memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'You shall do no work at all. This is to be a lasting ordinance for
the generations to come, wherever you live. It is a day of sabbath
rest for you, and you must deny yourselves. From the evening of the
ninth day of the month until the following evening you are to observe
your sabbath'" - Lev 23:31-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God repeats Himself here. No work at all. A sabbath rest. Deny
yourselves. He had already said it, and He says it again.

Repetition in Scripture is not carelessness. It is emphasis. God knew
how quickly His people would forget, how easily the most solemn day
could slide into an ordinary one within a generation.

Dear reader, we are no different. We forget faster than we expect. The
truth that moved us to tears last year can become a phrase we recite
without feeling. This is why God gave Israel a calendar of repeated
observances, and why the church has always returned again and again to
the same central truths.

Peter wrote that he would always remind his readers of these things,
even though they knew them and were firmly established in the truth (2
Pet 1:12). Jesus, instituting the Lord's Supper, said, "Do this in
remembrance of me" (Luke 22:19). He knew we would need reminding.

Do not despise the familiar. Do not think you have outgrown the basics
of the gospel.

Return to the cross today, even if you were there yesterday. Especially
if you were there yesterday.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which precious truths have become dull to me through familiarity?
2. What regular practice helps me remember what God has done?
3. Do I think I have moved beyond the basics of the gospel?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, I forget so quickly. Keep bringing me back to the cross, and
let familiar truths become fresh in my heart again. Amen.
